messages.subject: if statement control
parts:
Hi all, 
I am trying to analyse some distance sampling code from multiple transects, sites, years, and seasons but not every site in each transect is visited each year so I tried to set up the model in such a way that there was also an array in the constants that determined whether a specific site had been visited in that transect, year, season so the model would then only have to cycle over visited sites. But Im not sure if I can use if statements in this way, and having read other posts on here I think that indeed this doesnt work in NIMBLE?I have included a repoduceable example below. 
So I then tried to think of other solutions, and one would be to use a ragged array to only include the visited sites each year/transect/season but I also dont think NIMBLE will accept ragged arrays?
I have a site specific vegetation effect (as well as a season effect) that I would like to model on the observation probability hence the need to model at site level, I am also trying to use data augmentation at that level.. but that doesnt make too much difference to the functionality.
So if I cant use the 'if' in my NIMBLEcode I was wondering if anyone had any suggestions as to how I might be able to do this without asking the model to cycle through all the unvisited sites all the time uneccessarily?
Many thanks in advance for any advice,
Dave

Simplified example code:
library(nimble)

# Simulated data and constants
nTransects <- 3
nSeasons <- 2
maxSites <- 5
nSites <- sample(1:maxSites, nTransects, replace = TRUE) # Random number of sites per transect
site_visited <- array(sample(0:1, nTransects * maxSites * nSeasons, replace = TRUE),
                      dim = c(nTransects, maxSites, nSeasons))

observation <- array(rnorm(nTransects * maxSites * nSeasons, 0, 1),
                     dim = c(nTransects, maxSites, nSeasons))

# NIMBLE model
model_code <- nimbleCode({
  # Priors
  sigma_base ~ dunif(0, 100)  # Base value for sigma
 
  # Likelihood
  for (t in 1:nTransects) {   # Loop over transects
    for (s in 1:nSites[t]) {  # Loop over sites in each transect
      for (se in 1:nSeasons) {  # Loop over seasons
        if (site_visited[t, s, se]) {
          # Model logic here (simplified for example)
          observation[t, s, se] ~ dnorm(sigma_base, sd = 10)
        }
      }
    }
  }
})

# Constants and data (simplified for example)
constants <- list(nTransects = nTransects,
                  nSites = nSites,
                  nSeasons = nSeasons,
                  maxSites = maxSites,
                  site_visited = site_visited)

data <- list(observation = observation)

# Build and compile the model
model <- nimbleModel(model_code, constants = constants, data = data)

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: if statement control
parts:
Hi Dave,

I just wanted to confirm for you that you can't use an if statement nested in for loops in that fashion. If statements can only be used in a model to include/exclude a term in the model for the purpose of building multiple models from the same model code. 

It's fine to use ragged arrays such as this:

```
for(i in 1:n)
  for(j in 1:m[i])
    ...
```
though in your case, I'm not sure that is convenient in dealing with transects by sites by seasons.

One can also "flatten" the array so that you have a single loop over all the observations and you use nested indexing to determine the transect, site, and season associated with each observation.
For example there would be a vector (in constants) that specifies the season associated with each observation.

-chris
